comments.author: dundarious
comments.story_title: Anatomy of a Terminal Emulator
comments.why_zh: 关于高性能应用设计的 Refterm 系列
comments.quote_zh: Casey Muratori 的 refterm 视频系列是应用设计的一个绝佳示例。
comments.text_zh: Casey Muratori 的 refterm 视频系列是应用设计的一个绝佳示例。它聚焦于为 Windows 编写一个终端模拟器，但几乎所有概念也适用于类 Unix 系统——甚至深入到操作系统原语层面，比如用内存映射创建环形缓冲区等等。他构建了一个近乎完整的终端，看起来在 unicode 和转义序列支持上比 windows-terminal 更好，代码量却少得多，性能则真正高出几个数量级。我尤其喜欢他注重通过实验来确定合理的性能上限（这样你就能衡量成功/失败）、“非悲观化”（non-pessimisation，不做与实际任务无关的事）、理解实际机器及其能力（他不用这个说法，但有时被称为“机械同理心”），以及隔离你很可能不得不用（至少起步时）的“坏代码”的策略。[VIDEO]
comments.text: Casey Muratori's refterm video series is a great example of how to do application design. It focuses on writing a terminal emulator for Windows, but almost all the concepts apply to nixes as well -- even down to the level of OS primitives like memory mappings to create a ring buffer, etc. He builds a nearly complete terminal that appears to better support unicode and escape sequences than windows-terminal, in drastically less code and with literally orders of magnitude better performance. In particular, I like his focus on experimentation to figure out a reasonable upper bound on performance (so you can measure success/failure), "non-pessimisation" (don't do things extrinsic to the actual task), understanding the actual machine and its capabilities (he doesn't use the term, but sometimes called "mechanical sympathy"), and tactics for isolating "bad code" that you probably have to use (at least to get started). [VIDEO]

comments.author: grayrest
comments.story_title: 55 GiB/s FizzBuzz
comments.why_zh: Casey 关于 non-pessimization 的介绍
comments.quote_zh: Casey 最近关于 non-pessimization 的介绍
comments.text_zh: > 绝大多数慢代码之所以慢，并不是因为它没能做这类微优化，而是因为它用了错误的算法。我不同意。我认为大多数代码慢，是因为写的时候完全没有考虑性能。我喜欢 Casey Muratori 的 non-pessimization 理念：真正的优化（测量、处理热点）很少见，也很少有必要，但只要不采用本质上很慢的模式来写代码，就能相比当前普遍水平获得巨大提速。这不是什么深奥的算法内容，只是避免拷贝和/或指针追逐。编辑：[VIDEO] <- Casey 最近关于 non-pessimization 的介绍 > 对于现实规模的问题，如果由水平相当的程序员以相同的投入分别用 C 和 Python 写解法，Python 版本几乎肯定会更快。Advent of Code 每年都举办，我不确定 C 的情况（这不是我会关注的东西），但有很多 Rust 提交，虽然 Rust 提交出现得更晚，但并没有那么久。凭记忆，在几分钟的时间尺度上大约是 2 倍。Python 程序并没有更快。
comments.text: > The overwhelming majority of slow code isn't slow because it's failed to do this kind of microoptimization, it's slow because it used the wrong algorithm. I disagree. I believe the majority of code is slow because it's written without any consideration at all to performance. I like Casey Muratori's philosophy of non-pessimization where true optmization (measuring, working hot spots) is rare and rarely necessary but massive speedups compared to the general state of the art are achievable by simply not writing code using patterns that are inherently slow. This isn't deep algorithmic stuff it's just avoiding copies and/or pointer chasing. Edit: [VIDEO] <- Casey's most recent intro to non-pessimization > For a realistic-sized problem, if you write solutions in C and Python with the same amount of effort from equally skilled programmers, the Python version will almost certainly be faster The Advent of Code runs every year and I'm not sure about C (not something I track) but there are plenty of Rust submissions and while the Rust submissions take longer to come in, it's not THAT much longer. From memory it's like 2x on a timescale of minutes. The Python programs are not faster.

comments.author: hsn915
comments.story_title: Selecting a programming language can be a form of premature optimization
comments.why_zh: 解释 non-pessimization 与过早优化的区别
comments.quote_zh: 如果你想看对这个想法的进一步阐述，可以看看 Casey Muratori 关于优化哲学的讲座
comments.text_zh: 过早优化的谬误又冒出来了。Knuth 写那句话时，对“优化”一词有非常具体的所指：底层微优化。花大量时间试图从每条小小的 CPU 指令里榨出每一丁点性能。高层面的合理设计决策在这个意义上根本不是“优化”。你应该把它们看作 non-pessimization。选择 Python 或其他慢语言就是过早悲观化。你只是无缘无故让程序变慢。因此，根据用某种语言写出的程序表现来选择语言，就是 non-pessimization。如果你想看对这个想法的进一步阐述，可以看看 Casey Muratori 关于优化哲学的讲座：[VIDEO] 文章声称软件“足够快”，不需要进一步优化。但你所谓的“足够快”，可能比它本可以达到的速度慢 10000 倍。我没开玩笑。用慢语言编程的人对性能的认知严重扭曲。如果一个页面加载要 5 秒，他们不觉得这是问题。如果服务器响应一个请求要 500ms，他们不觉得这是问题。这简直不可接受。
comments.text: The fallacy of premature optimization rears its ugly head again. When Knuth wrote that quote, he meant something very specific with the word optimization: low level micro optimizations. Spending a lot of time trying to get every little ounce of performance from every little CPU instruction. High level reasonable design decisions are not "optimizations" in this sense at all. You should think of them as non-pessimization. Choosing Python or another slow language is premature pessimization. You just make your program slower for no reason. So choosing a language based on how programs written in it perform is simply non-pessimization. If you are interested in an expansion on this idea, checkout Casey Muratori's lecture about philosophies of optimization: [VIDEO] The article makes claims about software being "fast enough" and not needing further optimization. But what you call "fast enough" is probably 10000 times slower than what it could be. I'm not joking. People who program in slow languages have a really skewed perception about performance. If a page takes 5 seconds to load, they don't see that as a problem. If a server takes 500ms to respond to a request, they don't see that as a problem. This is simply unacceptable.

comments.author: jiggawatts
comments.story_title: Reclaiming the lost art of Linux server administration
comments.why_zh: Casey 解释为什么效率很重要
comments.text_zh: 我发现这在实践中是一种不成功的做法。性能是一件复杂、多面的事情。它有难以量化的隐藏成本。顾客会因为网站慢而厌恶地离开。如果某处有单线程瓶颈，再怎么“多堆几个核”也无济于事。超线性算法会越来越糟，其恶化速度很容易超过处理器速度的提升。值得注意的是，这是最近才出现的情况——几十年来单线程吞吐量一直指数级提升，所以许多管理员内化了一个观念：只要把有“仅仅二次方”扩展问题的应用迁到新硬件上，问题总会解决。现在……这毫无作用。我曾以高得咋舌的日薪作为顾问出现在许多站点，修复慢应用。无一例外，他们都缺一些微不足道的东西，比如数据库索引或缓存。不是 Redis 或那种花哨东西！只是静态内容上的缓存控制头。无一例外，从一开始就做对会更便宜。听 Casey 解释：[VIDEO] 你必须把效率放在心上、融入灵魂，否则不能诚实地称自己为工程师。好好学你的手艺，这样你就能以更少做更多——包括更少的开发者时间！
comments.text: I’ve found this to be an unsuccessful approach in practice. Performance is a complex, many-faceted thing. It has hidden costs that are hard to quantify. Customers leave in disgust because the site is slow. No amount of “throwing more cores at it” will help if there’s a single threaded bottleneck somewhere. Superlinear algorithms will get progressively worse, easily outpacing processor speed improvements. Notably this is a recent thing — single threaded throughout was improving exponentially for decades so many admins internalised the concept that simply moving an app with a “merely quadratic” scaling problem to new hardware will always fix the problem. Now… this does nothing. I’ve turned up at many sites as a consultant at eyewatering daily rates to fix slow apps. Invariably they were missing trivial things like database indexes or caching. Not Redis or anything fancy like that! Just cache control headers on static content. Invariably, doing the right thing from the beginning would have been cheaper. Listen to Casey explain it: [VIDEO] You need to have efficiency in your heart and soul or you can’t honestly call yourself an engineer. Learn your craft properly so you can do more with less — including less developer time!

comments.author: infogulch
comments.story_title: Making Code Faster
comments.why_zh: 让程序提速的三种模式
comments.quote_zh: 就是单纯避免给 CPU 增加额外的不必要工作
comments.text_zh: 我喜欢 Casey Miratory 在《优化的哲学》[1] [2] 里提出的「反悲观化」思路。他把「让程序跑得更快」拆成三种模式：（1）「优化」，包括计算预期周期或内存带宽、仔细做基准测试、设计定制算法等等，这可以很有趣，但代价高昂，而且很少被采用；（2）「反悲观化」，就是单纯避免给 CPU 增加额外的不必要工作，这本该 100% 做到，但今天的业界并没有；（3）「假优化」，就是肤浅地重复「优化小贴士」和来自无关的（1）类案例的结论，而不去实际测量。[1]：[VIDEO] [2]：[LINK]
comments.text: I like Casey Miratory's "non-pessimization" approach in Philosophies of Optimization [1] [2]. He breaks "making a program go faster" into 3 modes: (1) "optimization" which includes counting expected cycles or memory bandwidth, careful benchmarking, designing custom algorithms, etc which can be fun but is expensive and is only rarely applied; (2) "non-pessimization" which is simply avoiding adding extra unnecessary work for the cpu, which should be done 100% of the time but isn't in the industry today; (3) and "fake optimization" which is shallowly repeating 'optimization tips' and conclusions from unrelated cases of (1) without actually measuring it. [1]: [VIDEO] [2]: [LINK]

comments.why_zh: 非悲观化在实践中意味着什么
comments.quote_zh: 如果你想理解他这话是什么意思，就去看 refterm 系列。
comments.text_zh: 他不是说你应该花时间优化代码，而是说你应该从一开始就写出性能良好的代码，不要给 CPU 比完成任务所需更多的工作，通常是通过避免 OO 范式、遵循 SOLID 之类的东西等。然后如果需要，真正的优化可以处理代码中的热点，而且这通常只有组织里少数最好的工程师才能做对，但如果所有东西都很慢，那对这几个工程师来说就是一项无法完成的任务。如果你想理解他这话是什么意思，就去看 refterm 系列。[VIDEO]
comments.text: He isn't saying that you should spend time on optimising your code, rather that you should write performant code from the beginning by not giving the cpu more work than it needs to do to perform the task, typically by avoiding OO paradigms, followings things like SOLID, etc. Then if needed, real optimisation can handle the hotspots in your code and is typically something that only a few of an orgs best engineers can do properly, but if everything is slow then its an insurmountable task for these few engineers. If you want to understand what he means with this watch the refterm series. [VIDEO]

comments.author: DeathArrow
comments.story_title: For processing strings, streams in C++ can be slow
comments.quote_zh: 这里有一个关于软件速度的精彩演讲
comments.text_zh: 任何面向对象的东西都比过程式的东西慢。装箱和拆箱开销大，运行构造函数和析构函数开销大，复制对象开销大，虚表开销大。而且数据在内存里对齐得也不怎么样，可以预期会有大量缓存未命中和分支预测错误。最快的方式就是把 C 字符串放在一个数组里，然后对它跑一个函数。如果 OOP 有什么优点，速度肯定不是其中之一。这里有一个关于软件速度的精彩演讲：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Anything object oriented is slower than anything procedural. Boxing and unboxing is expensive, running constructors and destructors is expensive, copying objects is expensive, virtual tables are expensive. And stuff isn't aligned greatly in memory, we can expect lots of cache misses and branch mispredictions. The fastest possible way is to have C strings in an array and run a function over it. If there are advantages to OOP, speed is not one of them. Here's a great talk about software speed: [VIDEO]

comments.story_title: “Clean” Code, Horrible Performance
comments.quote_zh: 但首先，我们得确保我们的程序不会慢得像糖浆一样。
comments.text_zh: 我在为 Monocypher 实现 EdDSA 时意识到，优化是会叠加的。当我消除一个瓶颈后，我注意到代码的另一部分成了新的瓶颈，而且有些优化是以乘法方式叠加的。做了很多改动之后，我才终于开始遇到收益递减并停下来。而我一直把自己限制在标准 C99 内，还相当努力地避免在这上面花太多行代码。我的意思是，如果程序的大部分都被一大堆浪费掉的 CPU 周期拖慢（昂贵的抽象、慢速解释型语言……），那么那些本应显而易见的瓶颈很可能就淹没在一片性能低下的汪洋里。它们更难被发现，而且修掉它们也不会带来多大变化。所以，在你真正开始优化之前，程序应该已经快到让真正的优化能产生实际影响。是的，真正的优化应该很少做。但首先，我们得确保我们的程序不会慢得像糖浆一样。见 [VIDEO]
comments.text: I realised when I implemented EdDSA for Monocypher that optimisations compound. When I got rid of a bottleneck, I noticed that another part of the code was the new bottleneck, and some of the optimisations compounded multiplicatively . It took many changes before I finally started to hit diminishing returns and stop. All while restricting myself to standard C99, and trying fairly hard not to spend too many lines of code on this. My point being, if most of the program is slowed down by a slew of wasted CPU cycles (costly abstractions, slow interpreted language…), there's a good chance what should have been obvious bottlenecks get drowned in a see of underperformance. They're harder to spot, and fixing them doesn't change much. So before you even get to actual optimisation, your program should be fast enough that actual optimisations have a real impact. And yes, actual optimisation should be done quite rarely. But first, we need to make sure our programs aren't as slow as molasses. See [VIDEO]

comments.author: andai
comments.story_title: Fable Converted Pylint to Rust
comments.text_zh: > 你不可能在不真正消除很大一部分工作的情况下快 2000 倍。是的，正是如此。优化就是这样运作的！要认识到，在很多情况下，正在做的工作对于产生你真正需要的结果并不是必要的，它本来可以用另一种方式完成。这有时会涉及增加复杂性（通过更好的数据结构或算法，例如四叉树），有时会涉及去掉复杂性（非悲观化[0]）。话虽如此，通过破坏东西来实现加速当然也是可能的，而你是在暗示这里就是这种情况。那部分我无法评论。[0] Casey Muratori - Refterm Lecture Part 1 - Philosophies of Optimization [VIDEO]
comments.text: >You can't get 2000x faster without actually eliminating some large percentage of the work Yeah, exactly. That's how optimization works! Recognizing that in many cases, the work is that was being done is not necessary to produce the result you actually need, that it could have been in a different way. This can sometimes involve adding complexity (by means of a better data structure or algorithm, e.g. a quadtree), and sometimes involve removing it (non-pessimization[0]). That being said, it's certainly also possible to achieve a speedup by breaking things, which you are suggesting is the case here. I can't comment on that part. [0] Casey Muratori - Refterm Lecture Part 1 - Philosophies of Optimization [VIDEO]

comments.author: andai
comments.story_title: Overfitted a 900KB Transformer to Compress a 100MB CSV into 7MB
comments.text_zh: 前一阵我在做一个多人游戏，其中一版网络代码是“瘦客户端”，客户端只发送输入，服务器模拟游戏，并以 60Hz 把世界状态倒进管道里。我没有发布那个版本，但我估计那种做法会产生 3000 美元的带宽账单！我开始研究状态差分、压缩等等……直到我意识到，等等！我的玩家移动是线性的，所以我只需要一个开始和一个停止的数据包！于是我就实现了近乎无限的效率提升 :) 我想那个词是……专用解决方案可以胜过通用解决方案。还有，“记住程序实际需要做什么，然后让它就做那个”……我对网络代码做了非悲观化：[VIDEO]
comments.text: I was working on a multiplayer game a while ago, and one of the iterations of the netcode was "thin client" where clients just sent input, server simulated the game, and it dumped world state onto the pipe at 60hz. I didn't ship that version but I estimated a $3000 bandwidth bill with that approach! I started looking into diffing the state, compression, etc... until I realized, wait a minute! My player movement is linear so I only need a packet for start and stop! And so I achieved near infinite efficiency improvement :) I think the word is... a specialized solution can beat a general one. Also, "remembering what the program actually needs to do, and just making it do that"... I de-pessimized the netcode: [VIDEO]
